newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar/mark vols firm in short dates.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar/mark vols firm in short dates.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options rose Thursday amid lingering uncertainty about mark direction in the wake of Bundesbank criticism of Germany's plans to revalue its assets in reserve.
"There is buying interest in the short dates, because the market could go either way," said a senior dealer for a Japanese bank in New York.
One-month dollar/mark volatility climbed 0.3 point from the previous session to 9.80/10.10 percent Thursday and one-year rose 0.1 point to 9.45/9.70 percent.
"Traders were concerned about being caught short options volatility," said an analyst for a West Coast bank.
Market participants were inclined to seek protection against a breakout in the spot despite a relative lack of movement this session, traders said.
The dollar was weaker in the U.S. afternoon, trading around 1.6960 marks but holding above 116 yen.
The conflict over revaluation of Germany's gold and currency reserves erupted Wednesday when the Bundesbank issued a statement condemning the government's plan.
Mark/French volatility was bid up sharply, responding to the asset conflict in Germany as well as worry about the outcome of Sunday's second round of French parliamentary elections, traders said.
For one-month options, volatility rose to 3.20/3.60 percent in U.S. trading from 2.20/2.60 percent the previous session. Mark/lira volatilities climbed in sympathy.
In dollar/yen, one-month implied volatility was 11.30/11.50 percent, down from 11.40/11.70 percent, and one-year was steady at 10.30/10.50 percent.

Vols were drifting lower in dollar/yen as the spot held between 115.50 and 117.00 yen, but the market remains shaky after last week's steep decline, and that has kept the curve inverted, the Japanese bank dealer said.

The dealer predicted the volatility spread between short dates in dollar/mark and dollar/yen would narrow, with dollar/mark vols catching up to dollar/yen as political developments in Europe generate increasing uncertainty.
One-month 25-delta risk reversals remained skewed to yen calls at 1.0/1.3 and were 0.15 around par in dollar/mark.
